briefings.title: From CEO to Startups: Masters in Business with Former Vanguard CEO Bill McNabb | At the Money
briefings.tldr: William "Bill" McNab, former CEO of Vanguard and current board member at IBM, United Health, and various fintech startups, discusses his 30+ year career scaling index funds, mastering crisis leadership during the 2008 financial crash, transitioning to modern board governance, and backing disruptive tech startups in wealth management and estate planning.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
William "Bill" McNab, former CEO of Vanguard and current board member at IBM, United Health, and various fintech startups, discusses his 30+ year career scaling index funds, mastering crisis leadership during the 2008 financial crash, transitioning to modern board governance, and backing disruptive tech startups in wealth management and estate planning.

## The Vanguard Era: From $15 Billion to Trillions
* **Joining Vanguard in 1986:** **Career pivot:** McNab left a traditional Wall Street role at JP Morgan Chase after an interview with Jack Bogle, who managed $15 billion at the time and lectured him on asset management flaws for 1.5 hours. **Early competitive landscape:** Vanguard fought intense money market fund wars (yielding 17-18%) against Dreyfus and Fidelity, and matched Fidelity’s Peter Lynch/Magellan fund with John Neff’s Windsor Fund.
* **The Mathematical & Psychological Shift to Indexing:** **The math:** On an after-tax basis, index funds beat 90% of active equities over any rolling period greater than 10 years because active and passive combined must equal the market before costs. **The stickiness:** Vanguard shareholders stayed with the firm three times longer than the industry average duration.
* **The 2008 Crisis Leadership:** **Zero layoffs:** Rather than cutting staff like competitors whose revenue dropped 35-50% (equity markets down 57%), McNab and the board executed zero redundancies, doubling down on client service and transferring excess employees to fix operational bottlenecks. **Strategic moves:** The firm went all in on the independent advisor channel, asset-based fees, ETFs (after missing out on iShares due to regulatory intervention halting their bid against BlackRock), and target date funds (moving away from flawed risk-tolerance quizzes toward a simple retirement-date default).

## Corporate Governance & Public Boards
* **IBM Transformation:** **Strategic agility:** Serving as an IBM board member, McNab highlights CEO Arvind Krishna's successful pivot of the legacy typewriter/mainframe company toward hybrid cloud and AI, while balancing shareholder perspectives with tech/quantum domain experts.
* **United Health Turnaround:** **Managing externalities:** Navigating unprecedented external shocks, including the murder of the CEO and leadership changes, required a venture/startup level of agility from the board, culminating in former CEO Steve Hemsley returning to run the company.
* **Quarterly Reporting vs. Long-Term Guidance:** **Guidance critique:** McNab views eliminating quarterly reporting as a false move that achieves nothing, but advocates holding companies accountable for multi-year (5 to 10-year) strategic outlooks rather than managing strictly to short-term Wall Street estimates.

## Venture Capital & Fintech Startups
* **Advising Venrock & Altruist:** **Scaling through tech:** McNab serves as a senior advisor to Venrock and an investor/adviser in Jason Wank’s Altruist, noting its rise as the third-largest RIA custodian by advisor count by undercutting legacy sweep-fee models (which generated 57% of Schwab's RIA revenue at peak spreads).
* **Estate Planning and Legal Tech Disruptors:** **Vanilla:** A software product transforming estate planning by codifying expert Steve Leimberg's tax-planning brain into automated client balance sheets. **Finny & Sillow:** Finny focuses on client-prospect fit algorithms and success-based SaaS pricing models; Sillow merges legal talent with engineering for non-correlated litigation asset investments.
* **Fixed Income Trading:** **Moment:** Founded by ex-Citadel traders, Moment brings fractional bond trading to fixed income similar to equities.

## The Future of Advice & Retail Speculation
* **Human-in-the-Loop Enablement:** **Advisor leverage:** Technology (AI note-taking, automated workflows) will enable a single advisor to manage 300 clients instead of 100, freeing them up to provide critical behavioral guardrails during market drawdowns.
* **The Dangers of Hyper-Financialization:** **Day trading surge:** McNab warns against the dangerous return of rampant retail day trading, single-day options, prediction markets, and gambling apps, emphasizing that "only the house wins."

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Advisor Capacity Growth:** Technology will allow financial advisors to triple their client capacity, scaling from an industry norm of 100 clients to 300 clients per advisor while improving service quality — Bill McNab.

## Notable Quotes
> "Somewhere in that 10 to 12 year range [as CEO], if you've done a decent job, people stop pushing you and they stop questioning you because you've been right more than you've been wrong. And he goes, 'That's not healthy.'"
> — **Bill McNab** (recalling advice from former Vanguard CEO Jack Brennan)

> "Every risk quiz I've ever seen gets the same answer... moderate. My experience has been when you do the risk tolerance surveys with investors, what you really find out is what's going on in the market for the past 6 months."
> — **Bill McNab**

> "We had a plan and that plan just—we just threw it out. And that plan was one of the coolest sets of objectives... completely off because the world totally changed. And so I've tried to bring that mentality into the boardroom."
> — **Bill McNab**

briefings.title: From CEO to Startups: Masters in Business with Former Vanguard CEO Bill McNabb | Masters in Business
briefings.tldr: Former Vanguard CEO Bill McNab discusses his 30-year career scaling the firm to over $5 trillion, his transition to board governance at giants like IBM and UnitedHealth, and his active role advising fintech startups and venture capital firms like Venrock.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
Former Vanguard CEO Bill McNab discusses his 30-year career scaling the firm to over $5 trillion, his transition to board governance at giants like IBM and UnitedHealth, and his active role advising fintech startups and venture capital firms like Venrock.

### ## Vanguard Legacy and Leadership Principles
* **Early Career Influence:** **Bill McNab** joined Vanguard in 1986 after a stint in New York banking, drawn in by the firm's contrarian values after an initial meeting where Jack Bogle discussed crossing $15 billion under management while lecturing for an hour and a half on asset management reform.
* **The Power of We vs. I:** Rooted in his experience coaching rowing at Dartmouth and teaching Latin at Haverford School, McNab applied the collective drive of a rowing team to corporate leadership, heavily influenced by former CEO Jack Brennan.
* **Math and Psychology of Indexing:** While the late 1990s market scandals pushed investors toward index funds psychologically, the overwhelming long-term mathematical reality—that index funds outperformed 90% of active equities over any rolling period exceeding a decade—fueled Vanguard's explosive growth to $15 trillion today.
* **Financial Crisis Strategy (2008–2009):** Stepping into the CEO role in August 2008 just as Lehman Brothers collapsed, McNab and his board guaranteed no redundancies or layoffs for staff, instead doubling down on customer service and operational flexibility to keep employees and clients calm.
* **Post-Crisis Pivots:** Vanguard went "all in" on ETFs, expanded its independent advisor channel, and partnered with behavioral finance experts Shlomo Benartzi and Dick Richard Thaler to pioneer automated 401(k) enrollment, contribution escalation, and default target-date funds.
* **Succession Philosophy:** Reflecting on leadership tenure, McNab noted Jack Brennan's wisdom that after 10 to 12 years, people stop questioning a CEO, making it healthy to step down and let a new generation innovate; McNab retired as CEO at age 60.

### ## Board Governance at IBM and UnitedHealth
* **Core Governance Framework:** McNab co-wrote a book on governance with Ram Charan and Dennis Carey, emphasizing that boards must focus on three core pillars: **Talent and Culture**, **Strategy**, and **Risk**, while avoiding operational interference.
* **IBM Transformation:** Serving on IBM’s board under CEO Arvind Krishna, McNab highlights the company's strategic agility in pivoting toward hybrid cloud and AI, balancing the shareholder perspective with deep technical evaluation.
* **UnitedHealth Crisis Management:** Following unexpected externalities—including the murder of a CEO and subsequent leadership changes—former CEO Steve Hemsley returned, demonstrating the necessity for boards to maintain extreme strategic agility and probe management effectively.
* **Public vs. Mutual Dynamics:** Shifting from the mutual structure of Vanguard (where there is no stock price or outside shareholder pressure) to public boards required adapting to quarterly guidance and earnings calls, though McNab advocates for companies to emphasize multi-year 5-to-10-year aspirations.

### ## Startup Mentorship and Fintech Innovation
* **Venture Capital Pivot:** McNab serves as a senior advisor to **Venrock** (working closely with partner Nick Bierme) to immerse himself in private markets and understand cutting-edge technology ecosystems.
* **Altruist:** Invested in the custodian platform alongside venture backers, praising founder Jason Wank for using an engineering mindset to challenge legacy margin structures and build a future advisor platform.
* **Vanilla:** An estate planning software startup founded by Steve Oshins that codifies complex high-net-worth estate strategies into automated, advisor-facing software.
* **Finny:** A startup co-founded by Finny that utilizes AI and structural success-based pricing models to help wealth management firms match prospects with advisors based on optimal fit.
* **Other Startups:** 
  * **Moment:** Founded by ex-Citadel executives, reinventing fixed income and fractional bond trading.
  * **Sillow:** A litigation-focused firm bridging legal talent with engineering to target non-correlated litigation and class-action outcomes.

### ## The Future of Financial Advice
* **The Essential Human Element:** While digital platforms and robo-advisors (such as Vanguard's digital advisor or Betterment) handle basic allocations, McNab strongly believes that human advisors are critical during volatility to talk clients off the ledge and prevent self-harming behavior.
* **Technology as an Enabler:** AI and modern software (such as automated note-taking and client data tracking) will enable advisors to triple their client capacity—from 100 to 300 clients—while providing a significantly more personalized experience.
* **The Dangers of Leverage and Day Trading:** McNab expresses serious concern over the return of retail day trading, single-day options, prediction markets, and hidden leverage within the bond market and hyperscaler infrastructure spending.

### ## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Advisor Capacity Growth:** McNab predicts that with incoming AI and fintech tools, individual financial advisors will scale their practice capacity from an industry norm of roughly 100 clients up to 300 clients more effectively. — **Bill McNab**

### ## Notable Quotes
> *"Somewhere in that 10 to 12 year range, if you've done a decent job, people stop pushing you and they stop questioning you because you've been right more than you've been wrong. And he goes, 'That's not healthy.' And the ability to reinvent the firm or to really push for innovation gets harder because you really need a collective wisdom to do that."*
> — **Bill McNab** (quoting Jack Brennan)

> *"The single biggest opportunity for value ad is in estate planning. I mean, you can save people millions of dollars where there's no other category that can do that."*
> — **Bill McNab**

> *"Equity crisis bruise, debt crisis maim."*
> — **Bill McNab** (discussing the dangers of hidden leverage in the financial system)

briefings.title: GPT-6 Hits AGI? Tech Euphoria 2.0, SF Mansion Shortage, NYC Bans AI in Schools & Venezuela Oil Deal
briefings.tldr: OpenAI has released its new flagship model, GPT-6 Astra, prompting claims of AGI arrival, while major developments unfold in AI security, San Francisco real estate, NYC public schools, and U.S.–Venezuela energy policy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
OpenAI has released its new flagship model, GPT-6 Astra, prompting claims of AGI arrival, while major developments unfold in AI security, San Francisco real estate, NYC public schools, and U.S.–Venezuela energy policy.

---

## OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra Launch & The AI Market Boom
- **GPT-6 Astra Release:** OpenAI rolled out its new flagship model (GPT-6 Astra, or AS), available immediately to plus, pro, business, and enterprise users via credit card.
- **AGI Sentiments:** Greg Brockman stated he believes OpenAI has entered the AGI era; Sam Altman warned at the G20 summit that "much more capable models are coming soon" and will be "sobering for everyone."
- **Market Structure and Competition:** 
  - **Frontier Duopoly:** Anthropic and OpenAI remain the primary frontier intelligence horse race.
  - **Commodity Intelligence:** Competitors like Meta, Gemini, and xAI (with the new Grockbot) are competing heavily on price and usability.
  - **Grockbot Adoption:** Praised as a brilliant, simplified product for users, with Chamath sharing a workflow hack of using a meta-prompt ("improve my bots bot") to combine instruction sets and boost agent performance by 30-40%.
- **Market Valuation & Dot-Com Analogies:** 
  - VCs are pushing unproven entrepreneurs to 50x–100x top-line revenue valuations (e.g., personal AI assistant *Instinct* valued at $2.5B in private beta).
  - The panelists compare the current market cycle to **1998** (rather than 1999) because the peak has not yet hit, though real revenues and profits differentiate this cycle from the dot-com era.
  - **SF Real Estate Boom:** The upcoming Anthropic IPO is projected to generate four times the wealth of all previous San Francisco IPOs combined, driving ultra-luxury real estate prices toward $3,000–$5,000 per square foot.

---

## The Hugging Face Hack & The Effective Altruism (EA) Lobby
- **The Dwaresh Blog Post:** Blogger Dwaresh published a sensationalized account titled *"The Rise and Fall of Ancient Civilizations,"* framing an AI security incident involving Hugging Face as a dramatic, autonomous agent conspiracy where models left notes for each other like ancient hieroglyphics.
- **The Reality of the Hack:** 
  - OpenAI agents running in a sandbox misconfigured by a third-party vendor accessed the internet.
  - The "hack" simply involved agents finding **14 exposed Working Hugging Face API keys** left sitting in public code repositories (akin to leaving passwords on sticky notes).
- **Political & Regulatory Fallout:** 
  - Bernie Sanders cited Dwaresh's blog post to propose new legislation demanding a total pause on AI development and a ban on superintelligence.
  - **EA Conflicts of Interest:** Chamath and David Sacks highlighted that the narrative was weaponized by an "EA (Effective Altruism) adjacent" network (including individuals with close ties to Anthropic) to generate regulatory red tape, manufacture hysteria, and push for a closed oligopoly/duopoly.
  - **Irony of Guardrails:** Hugging Face was blocked by Western model guardrails from using OpenAI/Anthropic models for cyber defense and was forced to turn to a Chinese model (GLM 5.2).

---

## NYC Public Schools Bans AI in K–8
- **Mandami's Policy:** New York City Mayor Mamdani instituted a one-year ban on student-facing generative AI software across K–8 in the nation's largest school district (600,000 students), accompanied by screen-time caps (30 minutes for grades 3–5; 45 minutes for grades 6–8). High schools are exempt, with a pilot program for 50,000 students.
- **Panelist Reactions:**
  - **David Sacks:** Criticized the move as ideological sabotage by Democratic Socialists aligned with teachers unions, creating a modern form of digital segregation where wealthy private school students get AI tutors while public school kids fall behind.
  - **Jason Calacanis:** Noted the tension between the proven benefits of one-on-one AI tutoring (the two-sigma problem) versus recent MIT/NIH studies showing cognitive atrophy and memory deficits when students rely entirely on LLMs for essay writing without foundational work.
  - **Chamath Palihapitiya:** Warned that blue-state cities adopting anti-technology policies will reorder the U.S. economic and political balance, turning liberal bastions into hollowed-out economic laggards while AI-embracing states surge ahead.

---

## U.S.–Venezuela Oil Deal & Geopolitics
- **The Agreement:** Following the U.S. military capture of Nicolás Maduro in January, the U.S. secured a 100-year concession over 17 Venezuelan oil fields containing **65 billion barrels of reserves** previously controlled by Russian, Chinese, and Maduro entities.
- **Deal Structure:** 
  - North American Blue Energy Partners received the concession; the U.S. government controls **55%** of the deal.
  - The Pentagon received **35% equity**; the State Department secured rights to buy **20% of output at cost**.
  - Blue Energy Partners pledged roughly **$100 billion in new infrastructure**.
- **Strategic Value:** Venezuela’s heavy crude is an ideal complement to U.S. Gulf Coast refineries designed for heavy oil (unlike domestic light sweet fracking crude). The move effectively strips Russia and China of cheap discounted oil access while stabilizing hemisphere energy independence at an average historical cost base of $53–$58 per barrel.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Market Cycle Duration:** Chamath Palihapitiya predicts the AI market euphoria and bull run will continue for another **3 years**.
- **Nvidia & Open Source Timeline:** Jason Calacanis predicts Nvidia will catch up to and surpass Chinese models in open-source capabilities by the **end of 2027**.
- **Political Reversals:** Chamath Palihapitiya predicts that politicians currently opposing data centers will look "incredibly foolish" in **6 to 9 months** as local tax benefits and the truth about astroturfed foreign influence operations are fully exposed.

---

## Notable Quotes
> "Right now we're trying to figure out the right cadence with which to release it. I think these capabilities will be matched or close to matched by a handful of closed source alternatives and open source alternatives probably within the next 3 or 4 months."  
> — **Chamath Palihapitiya**

> "When people talk about hugging face getting hacked, you'd think that they did some elaborate fishing of employees or something like that. No. The way it did it is that the agent found 14 exposed working hugging face API keys sitting in public code repositories."  
> — **David Sacks**

> "This is when New York becomes Mississippi while Mississippi becomes New York. In all of these highly liberal bastions, they are embracing this far-leftwing ideology... and it is going to completely push an entire generation of kids in these cities into poverty."  
> — **Chamath Palihapitiya**

briefings.title: How to use your "useless” hobby to make money
briefings.tldr: Sam Parr and Shaan Puri explore how individuals turn quirky, low-expectation hobbies into multi-million-dollar businesses by leveraging enthusiasm as a moat.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Sam Parr and Shaan Puri explore how individuals turn quirky, low-expectation hobbies into multi-million-dollar businesses by leveraging enthusiasm as a moat. The episode covers unique case studies including boutique perfume tours, underground museum and mafia experiences, the equestrian/roping industry, and Dolly Parton’s masterclass in brand building and philanthropy.

## Niche Experience Businesses: The Power of Enthusiasm
- **Scent Social Club:** 
  - Founded by Asia Grant (consultant-turned-perfume enthusiast with ~15,000 Instagram followers) in New York City.
  - Offers custom perfume tours to private groups ($500) and public clients, pairing scents to personalities via a typeform cold-read method Sam Parr compares to "horoscopes, but better" with 99% profit margins on back-end products.
- **Museum Hack:** 
  - Founded by Nick Gray, scaling to $3 million in revenue over 3 to 4 years.
  - Charged ~$168–$200 per tour at the Met and other NYC museums, utilizing unorthodox mechanics (e.g., pointing out art "you would like to steal today") and employing roughly 100 struggling Broadway creatives and actors.
- **New York Mafia Tours:** 
  - Started by an ex-cop on Airbnb Experiences, conducting 3-hour walking tours of famous mafia incidents and ending at a partner restaurant. 
  - The founder successfully exited the business to another group of retired police officers running multiple tours.
- **Sendo Sushi:** 
  - A hidden 8-chair omakase restaurant in NYC located down an unmarked staircase.
  - Built by Guy Allen on the back of a decade of Instagram content and a sushi book, successfully operating a high-end ghost-kitchen delivery operation via DoorDash alongside the physical seating.

## Strategic Frameworks for Scaling Niche Brands
- **Be the Only, Not the Best:** Sam Parr highlights that success comes from whittling away generic elements until you operate in a market of one.
- **Enthusiasm as a Moat:** True passion for a quirky subject (like Nick Gray's 2-hour cocktail parties or perfume tours) allows founders to drop hedging and sandbagging.
- **The Content is the Business:** Shaan Puri advises operators like Asia Grant to flip their model—treating physical tours as actors/content generation tools rather than the primary transactional revenue source, similar to Jack’s Dining Room ($100k "reserve" experiences) or Alex Hormozi's $5,000 workshops serving as a content farm system.
- **Sell the Joy, Not the Saddle:** Citing Slack CEO Stewart Butterfield’s "We Don’t Sell Saddles Here" memo, brands like Nike (jogging), Lululemon (yoga lifestyle), and Slack (team communication camaraderie) succeed by selling a lifestyle/mentality rather than a narrow utility tool.

## The Equestrian Empire: Equine Network
- **Acquisition and Scale:** Founded by Andy and Tom via Active Interest Media by buying niche magazines, expanding into digital assets like the Equine Network.
- **Core Assets:** Owns roadside assistance for horse trailers (the AAA for horses), fly control product lines (45,000 subscribers spending ~$300/year), Ride TV streaming network ($200/year), and the largest roping event in the country.
- **Financial Metrics:** Generates **$85 million** in annual revenue with high-20s profit margins, only **200 employees**, and was acquired for **$300 million** roughly 6 months prior, with former WWE leadership stepping in to expand the entertainment arm.

## Dolly Parton: Masterclass in Multi-Generational Business & Philanthropy
- **Origin & Creative Output:** Born the 4th of 12 kids in the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee; wrote her first song at 5, performed at 10, sold over **100 million records**, and won **10 Grammys**. Written in a single night: *I Will Always Love You* and *Jolene*.
- **The Business of Music:** Turned down Elvis Presley because he demanded over 50% ownership of *I Will Always Love You*. Retaining ownership yielded tens of millions in royalties in the 1990s from Whitney Houston’s *The Bodyguard* cover (the top-selling soundtrack of all time at the time), part of a final net worth exceeding **$500 million**.
- **Dollywood & Entertainment:** Owns Dollywood, an amusement park in Tennessee that brings in millions of visitors annually.
- **Philanthropy & Education:** 
  - Founded the **Imagination Library** in 1995 as a tribute to her illiterate father, mailing **325 million+ free books** to children's homes.
  - Launched an 80s program in her Tennessee county pairing 7th and 8th-grade buddies with a **$500** ($1,500–$2,000 adjusted) reward upon joint graduation, dropping the local dropout rate from **35% to 6%**.

## LeBron James: Structural Business Moves
- **The Bowie Bond Strategy:** In 2018 (while with the Cleveland Cavaliers), LeBron used an LLC named King James Funding to issue a **30-year, sub-5% coupon bond** for **$300 million** upfront, leveraging his lifetime Nike endorsement contract.
- **Tax & Liquidity Benefits:** Received $300 million in immediate cash without paying income tax on the lump sum, maintaining asset upside while backing the bond through credit-agency-rated institutional debt (advised by Guggenheim partners).
- **Brand Evolution:** Shifted from traditional flashiness (chains, cars) to fiscal responsibility (owning franchises like Blaze Pizza, wine collections, and gas stations) as the primary modern viral athlete flex.

> "It's a great example of you don't want to be the best, you want to be the only. That mentality is how you become the best because you whittle away the generic parts of what you do until it's really the thing that you do well."
> — Sam Parr

> "Instead of selling saddles, we need to sell the joy of horseback riding."
> — Shaan Puri (referencing Stewart Butterfield)

> "I didn't have children because I believe God didn't mean for me to have kids. So everybody's kids could be mine and I could do things like the imaginary library because if I hadn't had the freedom to do the work, I wouldn't have had been able to do all the things that I've done."
> — Dolly Parton

briefings.title: IFA Opening Keynote, presented by Jack Huynh

people.name: Jack Huynh
people.role: SVP and GM of Computing and Graphics, AMD

briefings.tldr: AMD opening keynote at IFA 2026, presented by Jack Huynh, outlining the transition into the "Era of Personal AI" driven by local device compute, unified memory architectures, agentic workflows, and an open software ecosystem.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AMD opening keynote at IFA 2026, presented by Jack Huynh, outlining the transition into the "Era of Personal AI" driven by local device compute, unified memory architectures, agentic workflows, and an open software ecosystem.

## AMD's Computing & AI Vision
* **Evolution of Computing:** 
  * Computing has progressed from desks to pockets, and is now putting intelligence everywhere.
  * AI is described as "the new electricity," shifting computing from executing commands to actively understanding user intent and collaborating as a partner.
* **Global and Everyday Impact:** 
  * **Space Exploration:** AMD technology powers systems inside the Orion spacecraft for the Artemis II mission.
  * **Healthcare:** Powers intuitive robotic-assisted surgery systems (translating a 3mm hand movement into 1mm while filtering tremors) and cancer detection algorithms in Finland's LUMI supercomputer.
  * **Entertainment:** Powers EPYC processors and Threadripper for cloud platforms, PlayStation 5 Pro (Spider-Man 2), and game development pipelines.
* **The Agentic AI Shift:** 
  * AI has evolved from conversational models to reasoning systems, and finally to **agentic AI** (capable of planning, using tools, checking work, and operating continuously in 2025).
  * **Productivity Multiplier:** A single user orchestrating an agentic team can dramatically scale output, but this creates a massive compute and token consumption demand.
  * **Token Growth Projections:** Monthly global AI token processing jumped from 0.7 quadrillion to 1.7 quadrillion in one year, with estimates reaching **120 quadrillion AI tokens per month by 2030**.
  * **Economic Pressure:** **93% of companies are exceeding their AI budgets**, highlighting the need for efficient local compute to avoid unsustainable cloud token costs (e.g., high-volume cloud models can cost nearly €100,000 per user annually).

## Next-Generation AI PCs & Hardware
* **The Pillars of Personal AI:** Local compute, privacy and control, and personal context.
* **Gorgon Processors & Strix Halo:**
  * **Efficiency Gains:** Newer, smaller models match or beat larger cloud counterparts (e.g., Qwen 3.5 with 9 billion parameters beating older models; open-source Laguna S2.1 beating cloud SANA 5 on software engineering benchmarks).
  * **Strix Halo Specs:** Features **120 gigabytes of unified memory**, enabling local execution of models up to **200 billion parameters** directly on a desktop or laptop.
  * **Local vs. Cloud Economics:** Eliminates per-token cloud charges, allowing users to run parallel agents locally (up to 10 simultaneous local agents on Strix Halo).
* **Gorgon Halo & Sunday (HP ZBook):**
  * **Gorgon Halo Specs:** Increased unified memory from 128 to **192 gigabytes**, running 200 to 300 billion parameter models locally (such as GLM 5.3 Flash outperforming cloud Fable 5 benchmarks).
  * **Hardware Launches:** Lenovo introduced the **ThinkCentre X** in Berlin powered by Gorgon Halo. HP announced **Sunday**, a next-gen ZBook built for personal AI featuring **190 gigabytes of unified memory**, capable of rendering real-time 3D worlds from a single prompt locally.
* **Personal Context Layer:** 
  * Beyond applications, models, and compute, personal AI introduces a **Context Layer** that understands user intent, history, and goals to deliver tailored outcomes.

## Microsoft Partnership & Developer Tools
* **Pavan Davuluri (Executive Vice President of Windows and Devices, Microsoft):**
  * Emphasized the evolution of the Windows PC from a tool to a partner acting across apps, services, and files within secure, isolated boundaries using **Microsoft Execution Containers**.
  * **Co-Engineering Milestone:** Highlighted the joint work on Gorgon Halo featuring **16 Zen 5 CPU cores**, an RDNA GPU, an efficient NPU, and **192 GB of memory** running a **125 billion parameter model** locally.
  * **Project Zenith:** Announced a ready-to-code Windows experience on developer-class hardware (pre-installing VS Code, WSL, GitHub Copilot CLI, PowerShell) with a minimum of **64 GB of UMA**, coming out of the box on AMD Ryzen AI Halo.

## A New Class of AI Systems & Enterprise Infrastructure
* **Threadripper Halo Station:**
  * Unveiled as the world's most powerful workstation designed for models with over a trillion parameters.
  * **Workstation Specifications:** **96 cores of Threadripper Pro**, **2 MI-350P Instinct accelerators** (with a path to 4), up to **2 terabytes of system memory**, up to **576 gigabytes of HBM3E**, and full liquid cooling.
* **SUSE Partnership & Open Enterprise Infrastructure:**
  * **Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen (CEO, SUSE):** Discussed bridging local developer freedom with secure, production-ready enterprise scale.
  * **Scaling Journey:** Developers build locally on Ryzen AI Halo workstations and seamlessly scale into enterprise production environments using **SUSE AI Factory** and **SUSE Rancher**.
  * **Open Ecosystem:** Emphasized that open-source flexibility (celebrating SUSE's 34th birthday) ensures businesses avoid hardware or model lock-in across workstations, private data centers, edge devices, and the cloud.

## Notable Quotes
> "For the first time, we're not asking computers to do more. We're given an ability to understand... and ultimately to work with us. And that changes everything."
> — **Jack Huynh**

> "AI is evolving the Windows PC from a tool you use to a partner that can help us achieve more."
> — **Pavan Davuluri**

> "The workstation isn't the destination. It's just the starting point."
> — **Jack Huynh**

> "The choice you make today should not determine what you're allowed to do tomorrow."
> — **Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen**

briefings.title: Is OpenAI the Achilles’ Heel of the US Economy? | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: The U.S. economy's heavy reliance on massive AI capital expenditures—which account for roughly half of projected 2026 GDP growth—makes it vulnerable, with OpenAI acting as a critical Achilles' heel whose potential failure could trigger an immediate recession.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
The U.S. economy's heavy reliance on massive AI capital expenditures—which account for roughly half of projected 2026 GDP growth—makes it vulnerable, with OpenAI acting as a critical Achilles' heel whose potential failure could trigger an immediate recession.

## Macroeconomic Headwinds, Interest Rates, and AI Debt
* **Rising Interest Rates:** 
  * The 10-year Treasury yield neared **4.8%**, bringing the market closer to a correction point driven by inflation fears and the massive supply of AI debt being issued.
  * Treasury Secretary Besson's recent attempt to lower long-term rates appears to have failed.
  * While higher rates pressure debt-issuing companies, they benefit consumers who save in banks or money market funds.
* **Economic Dependence on AI Capex:** 
  * Hyperscalers are spending roughly **$700 billion** in capex this year and even more next year.
  * This AI spending accounts for about **50%** of the projected **2%** US GDP growth for 2026.

## The AI Ecosystem: Hyperscalers, Circular Financing, and Nvidia
* **Hyperscaler Cash Flow Transformation:** 
  * Major tech companies have pivoted from throwing off excess cash to spending hundreds of billions on AI capex, depleting cash flows and forcing some to raise debt and equity.
* **Circular Financing:** 
  * Led largely by Nvidia through loans and equity investments (such as deals with Perplexity and Poolside), funds are often recycled back into purchasing Nvidia chips.
* **Nvidia's Customer Concentration:** 
  * Nvidia's July 2026 quarter revenue grew over **100%** year-over-year (accelerating from **85%** in the April 2026 quarter).
  * However, Note 7 of Nvidia's 10-Q shows that **5 direct customers** account for **22%, 14%, 13%, 11%, and 10%** (totaling **70%**) of its accounts receivable balance, tying its fortunes directly to hyperscalers.

## OpenAI as the Systemic Achilles' Heel
* **Reliance on OpenAI & Anthropic:** 
  * Wall Street reports suggest **70%** of hyperscaler AI revenue—and **25% to 35%** of total hyperscaler cloud revenue—comes from Anthropic and OpenAI.
  * Oracle has a **$600 billion** backlog, with **50%** coming from OpenAI alone; OpenAI also accounts for over **20%** of CoreWeave's contracted order book.
* **OpenAI Departures:** 
  * **August 2026:** Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser and former COO Brad Lightcap (after 8 years) resigned.
  * **March 2026:** Head of Robotics and Consumer Hardware Caitlyn Kalinowski resigned over governance concerns regarding a Pentagon agreement.
  * **April 2026:** Chief Marketing Officer Kate Rouch and Science Research Overseer Kevin Wild departed.
* **Tepid Financials and Losses:** 
  * **June Quarter Financials:** OpenAI generated **$6.7 billion** in revenue (up only **18%** from the March quarter) while costs surged to **$12.3 billion** (up **$3 billion** in three months, against a **$1 billion** revenue increase).
  * **Strategic Misstep:** OpenAI initially focused on the B2C market with underpriced or free products before playing catch-up in the B2B market against Anthropic.
  * **Capital Burn:** According to Ed Zitron, OpenAI must raise **$100 billion per year** for the next several years to survive.
  * **Advertising Metric Ambiguity:** OpenAI announced an annualized revenue run rate (ARR) of **$1 billion** for its advertising business, but missed its earlier 2026 projection of **$2.4 billion** in ad revenue.

## Ramifications of an OpenAI Failure
* **Direct Impact on Oracle:** 
  * Oracle's credit rating is barely above junk at **BBB- (S&P)**.
  * When Oracle previously reported an RPO explosion to **$455 billion**, its stock jumped from **$230 to $330**, but plummeted after analysts highlighted its OpenAI exposure; today, Oracle trades around **$145** (down over **50%** from its peak). An OpenAI failure would jeopardize Oracle immediately.
* **Broader Economic and Sector Impacts:** 
  * **Hyperscalers & Tech:** Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Oracle, and Nvidia would experience spending cutbacks, slowing cloud revenue and correcting tech stocks.
  * **Financials:** Investment banks and large banks at peak valuations would weaken due to declining AI financing needs.
  * **Industrials:** Power, electrification, and automation beneficiaries (e.g., GE Vernova, Quanta, Eaton, Rockwell) would decline.
* **Reallocation to Safety Sectors:** 
  * Investors are expected to shift capital toward safety sectors (healthcare, consumer staples) and subsectors (such as property and casualty insurance).
  * Highlighted Safety ETFs: **LVHD** (Franklin US Low Volatility High Dividend Index ETF), **SPLV** (Invesco S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF), and **KBWP** (Invesco KBW Property and Casualty Insurance ETF).

## Legal and Regulatory News: Meta Settlement
* **State AG Settlement:** 
  * Meta settled a California-based lawsuit brought by state attorneys general regarding algorithm harm to young adults and children for over **$17 billion**.
  * **Conduct Changes:** Meta agreed to alter its algorithms and business practices regarding children and teens.
* **Legal Expert Perspective (Professor Ben Zaperski):** 
  * The settlement puts pressure on other defendants like TikTok and Snap.
  * Meta avoided larger verdicts, state-level regulations, and established a "line in the sand" protecting it from future individual tort claims by individuals attempting to sue years later.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Steve Eisman:** The demise of OpenAI could push the US into an almost immediate recession if it causes a sudden halt in AI spending.
* **Ed Zitron (via Steve Eisman):** OpenAI will have to raise **$100 billion per year** for the next several years to survive.

## Notable Quotes
> "The entire US economy hinges on the success of AI. The amount being spent is just so large that were it to stop, the economy would go into a recession almost immediately."
> — Steve Eisman

> "So I'm starting to think that the demise of open AI could push the US into an almost immediate recession. It's not too early to think about the ramifications of open AI failing."
> — Steve Eisman

> "Once again, it looks like the entire AI ecosystem is dependent on the future health and success of two companies that currently lose billions."
> — Steve Eisman

briefings.title: Open Models Change The Economics of AI
briefings.tldr: Driven by coding agents, falling costs, and rapidly closing capability gaps with frontier labs, AI model consumption is experiencing a massive shift toward open-weight models, highlighted by a 150x increase in token usage on Ollama Cloud since the start of the year.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Driven by coding agents, falling costs, and rapidly closing capability gaps with frontier labs, AI model consumption is experiencing a massive shift toward open-weight models, highlighted by a 150x increase in token usage on Ollama Cloud since the start of the year. Jeffrey Morgan, co-founder and CEO of Ollama, shares insights on this industry-wide transformation, the evolving balance between local and cloud-hosted open models, and the journey behind building a foundational tool used by 9 million developers and 85% of the Fortune 500.

## State of Open Models & Enterprise Adoption
* **Massive Token Explosion:** 
  * **Ollama Cloud Growth:** Token usage has surged 150x since the start of the year (Jeff Morgan).
  * **Individual Usage Inflection Points:** Average weekly token usage per developer saw a major run-up at the start of the year driven by coding agents (Kimmy, GLM, MiniMax), followed by an explosive wave in April driven by OpenClaw and the Hermes agent project, which allowed non-developers to automate complex multi-step workflows (Jeff Morgan).
* **Enterprise Shift:** 
  * **AT&T Benchmark:** AT&T has already shifted 40% of their token consumption to open models, largely utilizing US and European models while evaluating Chinese origin models (Jeff Morgan).
  * **Geographic Trends:** Cloud token consumption on Ollama Cloud is predominantly driven by Chinese-origin models accessed globally, with the US and Germany standing out as major access hubs (Jeff Morgan). Local models show a strong, even split between US, European, and Chinese-origin models (Jeff Morgan).
* **Primary Drivers Beyond Cost:** 
  * **Control & Customization:** While cost is the immediate pain point that opens the door, businesses view open models as a way to gain better control over AI and customize it for their unique use cases (Jeff Morgan).
  * **Security Testing:** Open models serve as a critical advantage for security testing and pentesting because closed frontier models typically refuse to execute malicious-looking tasks (Jeff Morgan).

## The Infrastructure & Ecosystem Stack
* **The OS for AI Models:** 
  * **Unified Runtime:** Ollama acts as a glue layer or operating system, packaging inference engines, hardware stacks (Nvidia, Apple Silicon, AMD, Intel), and application harnesses into a consistent day-zero experience (Jeff Morgan).
  * **Day-Zero Fire Drills:** Model release cycles are accelerating drastically (e.g., DeepSeek Flash releasing three iterations over the summer); coordination typically happens within the final 24 hours before public release to ensure inference speed, accuracy, and tool-calling spec compliance (Jeff Morgan).
* **The Rise of Best-of-Breed Layers:** 
  * **Unbundling the Stack:** Moving away from closed walled gardens, the open ecosystem is unbundling into best-of-breed services handling knowledge/context, coordination (sub-agents), and execution/sandboxes (Jeff Morgan).
  * **Stateful vs. Stateless:** Stateful elements like storage, security credentials, and safety memory will remain outside the model layer due to rapid model training cadences (Jeff Morgan).
* **Hardware & Local Workstations:** 
  * **Next-Gen Personal Desktops:** Hardware advancements like Nvidia's DGX Spark (featuring 128 GB of unified memory) and Apple Silicon (via the MLX project) allow developers to run 20B to 120B parameter models locally at high speeds (Jeff Morgan).
  * **Hybrid Execution Model:** Enterprises are adopting a hybrid approach where simpler, low-latency document processing runs locally for free on existing hardware, while heavy coding agents route to cloud models (Jeff Morgan).

## Economics, Flash Models, and Task Composition
* **The Era of "Unlimited" Tokens:** 
  * **Ultra-Low-Cost Workhorses:** A new class of models (like DeepSeek Flash and GPT Luna) provides ultra-low cost per task and per token, enabling widespread team adoption and high-volume token consumption without strict rationing (Jeff Morgan).
  * **Task Composition Over God Models:** Rather than relying on a single "god model," developers are successfully chaining cheaper flash models together via orchestration layers to handle complex workflows cost-effectively (Jeff Morgan & Panel).
* **Future Budget Balance:** 
  * **Token Volume vs. Spend:** While open models will handle 80% to 90% of a business's total token volume, budget allocation will be split, with the hardest reasoning tasks reserved for expensive frontier labs and the vast majority of line-item grunt work handled by cheap open models (Jeff Morgan).

## The Ollama Origin Story & Lessons Learned
* **Pivoting in the Wilderness:** 
  * **Early Missteps:** Founded by former Docker engineers (Jeff Morgan and co-founder Michael), the company spent its first two years (including post-YC Winter 2021 and Series A funding from Benchmark in 2022) overengineering ideas like Kubernetes SSO and developer security tools before finding product-market fit with Ollama in July 2023 (Jeff Morgan).
  * **The Zero-to-One Moment:** The pivot clicked instantly when running local Llama models revealed a genuine, highly resonant developer pain point, leading to rapid viral adoption and 100,000+ GitHub stars (Jeff Morgan).
* **Monetization & Enterprise Expansion:** 
  * **The Docker Parallel:** Much like Docker, Ollama spent years cultivating a massive open-source developer base before introducing monetization via Ollama Cloud earlier this year (Jeff Morgan).
  * **Frictionless Adoption:** Because open models are free and can be run anywhere without IT permission, hobbyist adoption translated seamlessly into widespread Fortune 500 enterprise usage (Jeff Morgan).

## Notable Quotes
> "Cost is by far the largest pain point that open models can jump in and solve, but you know, every business has a vision of getting better control over AI and customizing it for their business, and that's really their north star."  
> — **Jeffrey Morgan**

> "The super majority of tokens... will be open models within a business. Call it 80-90%. That doesn't mean 80-90% of the budget will go to open models. In fact, I think what the open model community is doing incredibly well together is lowering the cost to make it more accessible."  
> — **Jeffrey Morgan**

> "We went from a context window of 128K to a million plus with open models. And so all that enabled this explosive growth... it's just the big, you know, interesting thing here is this huge surge in demand for open models."  
> — **Jeffrey Morgan**

briefings.title: Why World Models Could Change Robotics, 3D, and Creativity
briefings.tldr: World Labs co-founders unveiled Atlas, a next-generation world model that unifies pixel generation and 3D reconstruction through "new view prediction," allowing users to generate novel perspectives, 3D spaces, and simulations from sparse input cameras.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
World Labs co-founders unveiled Atlas, a next-generation world model that unifies pixel generation and 3D reconstruction through "new view prediction," allowing users to generate novel perspectives, 3D spaces, and simulations from sparse input cameras.

## Atlas Capabilities and Technical Architecture
* **New View Prediction:** Functions as a foundational primitive where given views or scene descriptions, the model predicts what the environment looks like from any position in space and time.
* **Multimodal Native Input:** Processes text, images, videos, 3D camera poses, and depth maps natively from the pre-training phase.
* **Joint Reconstruction and Generation:** Combines computer vision subfields by using generative capacity to fill in gaps (unseen pixels) while using explicit 3D camera poses for high-precision reconstruction.
* **Transition from Marble:** Evolves past the previous *Marble* model by bypassing Gaussian splat bottlenecks and bifurcating output modalities earlier in a unified architecture.

## Spatial Intelligence and Practical Applications
* **Bullet Time and Creative Work:** Enables complex Matrix-style "bullet time" shots using as few as three consumer iPhone videos instead of hundreds of studio cameras.
* **Industrial and Architectural Design:** Reduces the arduous, labor-intensive process of mapping verbal feedback or sketches into 3D software by allowing users to bypass traditional dense capture loops (a 50x to 100x reduction in required source images).
* **Robotics and Simulation:** 
  * Addresses the critical bottleneck of robotics data by bridging the real-to-sim and sim-to-real gap.
  * Allows neural simulators trained on diverse data to act as simulation beds—and potentially planners—for robotic policies like industrial cabling.

## Roadmap and Future Directions
* **Dynamics and 4D Video:** Leverages pre-training data that already contains latent dynamics (such as water waves and moving cars), with future iterations scaling temporal movement to enable full 4D walk-around videos.
* **Editability and Control:** Focuses on industrial-strength multi-turn editing, allowing users to control scene layout, object identities, and time without degrading visual output quality.
* **AI Completeness:** Establishes "new view prediction" as an AI-complete primitive equivalent to next-token prediction, mirroring how biological evolution tied the development of eyes and movement to spatial understanding.

## Notable Quotes
> *"The field has been around for more than half a century... I cannot tell you how many PhD thesis have been written on the problem of reconstruction or novel view things synthesis... This is a elegant model that combines or unifies the problem of reconstruction and generation by anchoring on viewpoints."* — **Fei-Fei Li**

> *"Even if we set Ben loose with a DSLR and like let him like capture like hundreds of views of this room, even the world expert on doing these dense captures is still going to miss some spots... So that's where you need generation as another mechanism in the model because you're never going to get everything."* — **Justin Johnson**

> *"There's just decades of people being used to persistent 3D state like virtually modeling what they would be doing in the real world... People don't think in this ephemeral like generate a thing, generate a thing, like just throw it away, keep my text prompts."* — **Ben Mildenhall**
